# Decisions

Numbered, dated, never renumbered. A later decision that reverses one says so and links back. When code and this
file disagree, fix one of them in the same change. Gaps in the numbers (D496–D499, D525–D539) are ranges handed to
parallel branches that took fewer; they stay unused.

This file is the record and too long to read in a sitting: start from [DECISION-INDEX.md](DECISION-INDEX.md) (one
line per decision with its status) and [DEAD-ENDS.md](DEAD-ENDS.md) (every killed idea by topic). Both are generated
from this file (D812): after adding or changing a decision, run `bun run decisions:index`; a test fails while they are
stale. After a merge or rebase that touches DECISIONS.md, run `bun run decisions:index`; never hand-resolve the
generated pages (`.gitattributes` merges them as a union so a merge never stops on them).

Departures from the plan: no new `ContextualBandit` primitive, no capability probe (the cascade and the incumbent learn from real lookups), immediate reward only. When a search tool has no `args` function, `McpSource` maps the call from its input schema plus operator-fixed values, and refuses a schema it cannot map rather than guessing. It runs only for connectors that served normally, draws on its own rate bucket at half serving's rate and burst and waits while serving's is empty, so it never takes serving's tokens but can send a connector up to 1.5x serving's rate (`SourceFanout.permitShadow`), feeds rate-limit errors back, runs one lookup per session at a time, learns, and reports content-free `ShadowRecord`s with sanitized item ids to `onShadow`. (1) `cardsLean` (with `cardsLeanDays` 30): an item the card prefilter rejects is read for intent requests only when it is not automated (`automated`: a no-reply, notification or list sender in its `From:` line or `meta.from`/`meta.sender`, a bulk category, a bulk footer) and is dated within 30 days or upcoming (`readForIntent`). (2) `syncPush` (with `syncPushMaxStaleMs` 24 h): a synced source whose integrator forwards change notifications (`Source.notifies`, `notifies` in a user's MCP source spec) is behind only when told (`ContextPartner.sourceChanged`, `POST /v1/sources/changed`, the client's `sourceChanged`) and is then polled once by the next lookup that reads it; notifications that carry items are stored as synced after the secret gate with no call (`sourceItems`, `POST /v1/sources/items`, at most 100 items, checked by `checkSourceItems`). It is polled anyway after 24 h with no notification (a lost one is bounded) and by the daily sweep; sources that do not notify are polled as before (D57, D63, D101 unchanged for them), and a notification for one is ignored (`synced: false`). A poll does not take items pushed since its last complete poll for the point where its listing reaches what was synced; a notification during the backfill's last page leaves the copy behind once warm. Inert until an integrator declares a notifying source. (3) `askReaderCoalesceMs` (parallel asks of one session and request sharing one reader call over the union of their pools) is deleted with its code and tests, as D116's reuse was. (4) No change for prompt-cache placement: Pi's provider layer sends Eden's packet after the cached system prompt and tools; the lower cache-read share with Eden is fewer agent turns. Parts: `cardsLean` belongs to `cards` and `intent`, `syncPush` to `sync` (`docs/profiles/minus-*.json` updated). A packed item's `text` is an own enumerable getter over `Bun.deflateSync` bytes (Latin-1 bytes decoded with `latin1` when every character fits, else UTF-8), so spreads, `JSON` and `structuredClone` are unchanged; text under 256 characters or that shrinks by less than a fifth stays plain; a 256-entry process-wide memo keyed by each item's own bytes serves repeated reads. `put` indexes, tallies and graphs the plain copy and holds the packed one; a refresh with the same words keeps the held bytes (`repackLike`); text with a lone surrogate stays plain (UTF-8 would turn it into U+FFFD, and every refresh would then re-index it). The memo is cleared by `forget` and `removeItems`; after an expiry or eviction a decoded text can stay in it until 256 newer decodes push it out (never reachable from another item). Named `packText`, not `compactText`, which is `render.ts`'s cut of text to the cue. Why reverse D187: a SigV4 presigned URL is a bearer capability for up to 7 days (its `X-Amz-Expires` cap), granting a read or a write of a private object to whoever holds it, and Eden stores, indexes and sends to a model the text it gates; an expiry does not make that safe. The New Relic rule is one regex; the presigned rule finds the parameter name by regex and reads the value by a walk over its characters, each walk ending where the next name can begin. (b) The proxy path worked first time but failed silently: a request naming no user is now said once on stderr (no content); `GET /healthz` is the proxy's own; an upstream with no version path is warned about; one `/v1/whoami` probe at startup says whether Eden is reachable and takes the key. (c) Every server configuration mistake (short or missing `EDEN_API_KEYS`, busy port, missing sources file, unwritable `EDEN_HOME`) printed Bun's source excerpt and stack with the message buried; now one `eden: …` line, exit 2 (with several processes the router's startup failures go through the same line, after any child's own line). Both clients' transport errors name where they were sending (`eden /v1/events: cannot reach http://127.0.0.1:8790 (…)`), where the runtime said only "Unable to connect"; every URL in the line, the runtime's message included (Node's fetch quotes a URL with credentials), loses its `user:password@`, query and fragment (`redactUrls`, `redact_urls`), as do the proxy's own log lines. An answer that arrived but could not be read is reported as such, not as "cannot reach". Docs: README (what the quickstart's answers mean, installing from another repo, the proxy's `EDEN_API_KEY`/`EDEN_URL`/`PROXY_PORT`, an honest status line), INTEGRATION.md (proxy settings, TS install, hosting: key generation, the container path of the users file, Bearer only), the Dockerfile header. | D371  | 2026-11-07 | **The sync's per-source ids are an `IdSet` (`@eden/primitives`; A24).** A frozen user (D325) still held one string per synced item in `SourceSync.ids` (~250 KB at the 3,000-item cap). `IdSet` keeps `Set<string>`'s semantics (insertion order, deletes during iteration) in typed arrays: a Latin-1 byte arena with an escape for wider code units, per-slot start, hash and live flag, a 16-bit open-addressed table (32-bit past 65,534 slots) at most three quarters full, compaction never under an open iterator. The directory is capped (`EDEN_PERSIST_MAX_MB`, default 4,096): a freeze past it is not written. Why opt-in: it trades D8's "nothing on disk" for restarts that do not re-read every source; the key beside the files means a host compromise reads persisted users, which an operator must choose, not inherit. A deployment setting, not an engine behaviour: no trial row (D112 governs `DEFAULT_CONFIG`, which is unchanged). | D991  | 2026-11-11 | **Persistence on by default (the owner's decision on D863's recommendation; departs from D8 and from D425's opt-in).** Idle users are written to disk, encrypted, with no setting but the key: `EDEN_PERSIST_KEY` (the operator's 32 bytes) is required, and startup stops with one `eden:` line naming it and `EDEN_PERSIST=off` when it is missing. No key is ever generated: one stored beside the files would protect nothing (D863's condition 1). `EDEN_PERSIST=off` is the explicit way out and refuses `EDEN_PERSIST_FROZEN_DIR`, `_KEY` or `_MAX_MB` beside it; `EDEN_DEV=1` with none of them set stays off (local, no real users; requiring a key there would break `bun run dev`, the demo and every dev-mode test, and dev mode warns beyond loopback). The directory defaults to `$EDEN_HOME/frozen` (`/data/frozen` in the image). Its cap defaults to the machine's memory, lowered to a visible cgroup limit, at least 4,096 MB (`defaultPersistMb`, `machineMemory`; D863's condition 2): users are bound by memory (2-4.4 MB RSS a user at the cap) and a user's file is smaller (compact 0.8-1.2 MB, warm 1.8-2.7 MB), so the cap holds a file for every user the box serves. Every child's listening line says whether users are persisted, with the count on disk and the cap. A shutdown that wrote nothing no longer logs "persisted 0 live users" (a router's failed start had buried its cause under one such line a child). D863's condition 3 (D652, disk only) was deleted by D817 and is not revived here. THREAT-MODEL (assets, T12) and PRIVACY say content is at rest, redacted and encrypted, in every deployment. Tests and benches that start a non-dev server without measuring persistence set `EDEN_PERSIST=off`. | D992  | 2026-11-11 | **More than one machine, built (D864's design, refreshed).** Users are placed by a 16-bit unkeyed bucket of tenant and user (`bucketOf`, @eden/protocol). Machines own buckets by rendezvous hashing over node ids (`OwnerTable`, @eden/primitives): adding a node moves about 1/(n+1) of users, all to it, and losing any node moves only its users, each to its second choice (jump hashing could only drop the last node, so it serves the children instead: `childTable`, which replaces `childFor`'s `mod N` and moves 1/(N+1) of users when a child is added). Persistence files are named `<bucket>-<keyed hash>.blob` in one directory per machine; each child indexes only its own buckets, so a new child count moves nothing on disk (the old `<i>-of-<N>` directories are deleted once; nobody had them: the image could not start before D990). `SharedFrozenDisk` (engine) mirrors each file, byte for byte and still encrypted, to an S3-compatible store (`S3BlobStore` on Bun's built-in client, no new dependency; `EDEN_PERSIST_STORE`), fetches a user it does not hold before their first read (`FrozenDisk.fetch`, awaited by `ItemCache.ready`: the wait is that request's, never the event loop's), keeps the store's copy at a thaw (the failover copy: the last compact freeze, release or shutdown) and deletes it on forget, expiry and eviction; a node starts with its local files cleared, so a local file is never older than the store's. The persisted blob carries the user's source-map rows (`SourceMap.exportUser`/`importUser`, `PERSIST_FORMAT` 5). The cluster router (`cluster.ts`, `EDEN_NODES` or `EDEN_NODES_FILE`, re-read on SIGHUP) routes by bucket; a membership change is planned: every live node is told (`POST /internal/cluster`, `EDEN_CLUSTER_KEY`), releases the users it no longer owns (`ContextPartner.releaseMoved`: written with sync state and rows, handed to the store, dropped here) and only then does routing switch; moving users get 503 with Retry-After meanwhile. A node failing `/readyz` three probes in a row (2 s apart) is dropped at once and its users' new owners fetch their last stored blob; it comes back the planned way. Measured on one host (`bench/cluster.bench.ts 300 100 1000`, 3 nodes, in-memory store; one run): adding a fourth node moved 24.8% of buckets and released 97 users in 173 ms, removing it the same in 56 ms; a killed node was routed around 4.6 s after the kill; latency at 100 events/s, direct to the owning node against through the router, p50 1.37/1.12 ms against 1.42/1.22 ms and p99 4.53/4.36 against 5.96/4.98 (two runs each). At full size (`bench/release.bench.ts`: 3,000-item prose users, a sixth live and the rest warm, a store at 30 ms a call): one process released 60 users in 422 ms and 120 in 1.65 s (live about 30 ms each, warm 3-7 ms), in the store within 0.7-2.4 s; a new owner fetched and thawed 60 in 1.44 s. Tests: placement, the router's N 2 -> 3 -> 2 with persistence on (every user read back by its new child, none re-synced), the shared store with an in-memory store, `S3BlobStore` against an S3 stand-in (`fixtures/fake-s3.ts`), and three machines end to end (`cluster.test.ts`: placement, a node added, killed and removed, forget). Not built: a shared ledger of per-tenant spend (D993), live resizing of a machine's child count (a restart, as before). | D995  | 2026-11-11 | **Fencing and forget across machines (the reviewer's findings on D992-D994).** (1) A whole-user forget that lands while a moved user's blob is being fetched cancels the fetch (a per-file generation), so the bytes are not adopted and the user does not come back. (2) Forgetting one source, or items deleted at their source (`removeItems`), deletes the store's copy (`FrozenDisk.invalidate`), so a failover cannot serve a revoked connector's items. (3) Membership messages carry an epoch (wall-clock based, so a restarted router is newer) and a mode: `release` for planned changes, `drop` for a failover, where the other nodes, and the lost node as far as it can be reached, discard users they no longer own without writing them. A node taken out (it stopped answering, or did not answer a release) is told to drop everything before it is admitted again, so a node that stalled and resumed never serves its pre-outage copies (end to end: a node frozen with SIGSTOP, resumed, held 0 users before its users were handed back from the store; with both the drop and the reset disabled the test fails). With a table a node fences itself: an API request for a user another machine owns gets 503 "not the owner", and nothing of such a user is written to or deleted from the store (`SharedFrozenDisk.setWritable`). (4) A node whose `/readyz` says draining is a planned leave: it hands its users over before the router moves them. (5) A cluster node that persists needs `EDEN_PERSIST_STORE` (startup refuses otherwise). (6) `loadConfig` derives default paths from the env it is given. (7) A release drops the user's gone-holds and closes their connections (`UserSources.forget`). (8) A single machine with a store sweeps its own copies. Left as is, documented: a store write still pending when a release times out (the router logs the count; that user may start from the older copy). | D1070 | 2026-11-11 | **Release readiness (R1, docs/research/r1-release.md): the deploy kit's correctness fixes; amends D994 and D995.** (1) A machine router's plain `/readyz` is ready while any child is up (503 when none is, or draining); `/readyz?all=1` keeps D994's every-child rule and is what the cluster router probes. Before, one crashed child made the single box's Caddy mark the whole of Eden unhealthy. (2) A fenced process (D995) drops its own queued store write of a name when a delete for it arrives, and a store write that starts (or retries) after its bucket is fenced is skipped: a late put could land after the new owner's delete of a forgotten user, or over its newer copy. A put already on the wire when the fence moves still lands (one store call's window). (3) `SharedFrozenDisk.absent` holds at most `MAX_ABSENT` (100,000) names, then starts over (one store read a user). (4) A release message that finishes after a newer membership no longer puts its older table back. (5) A machine router replays the last membership to a child that (re)starts, before it serves; a membership sent meanwhile reaches the replaying child too, and the replay sends it if it began first. (6) The cluster router gives up on a forwarded request after 60 s (503). (7) `Ops.wrap` answers any throw with 503, and `main.ts` has a 503 `error` handler; a membership naming more than 1,024 distinct nodes is a 400 (placement builds its table on the event loop). (8) The router kills a child 1.25x the grace after its SIGTERM, not at the grace its steps fill. No engine behaviour changes: eval and funnel unchanged. | D1071 | 2026-11-11 | **A persistence key that opens none of the persisted users stops the start (the parent's decision on R1's finding; amends D425 and D991).** Before, a mistyped `EDEN_PERSIST_KEY` on an upgrade started ready and deleted every blob. Now each process's open (`EncryptedFrozenDisk`, `refuseForeignKey`) throws `PersistKeyMismatch` when its directory holds blobs of its buckets and the key opens none of them (an expired blob of the key counts as opening), deleting no foreign blob; with `EDEN_PERSIST_STORE` the store holds a marker of the key (`<prefix>key-id`, the 8-byte key id every blob header carries; `SharedFrozenDisk.verifyStoreKey`): another key's marker stops the start, and a store with no marker yet is sampled (up to 8 blobs, all foreign stops it) before the marker is written. A sample alone would refuse the right key after a rotation, since the old key's blobs stay until the 7-day age sweep (the review). The check is bounded at 3 s: a store that fails or hangs does not block the start. The server exits 2 with one line naming `EDEN_PERSIST_KEY` and `EDEN_PERSIST_DISCARD=1`. `EDEN_PERSIST_DISCARD=1` keeps the old behaviour (a rotated key: discarded, re-synced; the store's marker moves to the new key) and says so. A store where some blob opens starts and discards the foreign ones, as before; an unreachable store does not block a start. Also R1's lows pinned by tests (the 1.25x kill, the 503 `error` handler, the shutdown flush, the turn-gate notice), and an unknown path is 404 whatever the method (a route asked with GET stays 405). | D1704 | 2026-11-12 | **Adopted (the owner's request; D1701's first candidate): Eden speaks MCP through its own minimal client, streamable HTTP transport and `ask_context` server; `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` and zod are devDependencies only.** `packages/sources/src/mcp/` holds the JSON-RPC types (its `Transport` is shaped so the SDK's transports fit it unchanged), `McpClient` (`initialize` with version negotiation over the SDK's five versions, paged `tools/list`, `tools/call`, the SDK's 60 s timeout, `notifications/cancelled` on abort or timeout, `McpError` messages as the SDK's, `ping` answered, at most 16 at once, and every other server request (sampling, roots, elicitation) dropped unanswered: each answer is a POST with the user's credentials), `StreamableHttpTransport` (JSON and SSE replies, `Mcp-Session-Id` kept and checked as visible ASCII, `Mcp-Protocol-Version` after `initialize`, a 404 on a held session closes the transport so `McpSource` re-initializes) and a one-pass SSE parser over bytes. Bounded and defensive: every POST has a deadline (60 s) and is aborted at it or at close; a reply is read up to 16 MiB (JSON and SSE; 4 MiB for `tools/list`, 4 MiB for one SSE line or event) and cut past it; a reply carrying over 100 malformed or unasked messages, or over 100 server requests, is failed with one error; a 202 to a request fails at once; a leading BOM is dropped; an unended SSE line is kept as parts and joined once (joining per chunk was quadratic); JSON passes `bodyShapeUnder` (D100) before `JSON.parse`; only the response whose id is the POSTed request's is taken from a reply (a numeric id echoed as a string counts, as the SDK's client accepts); a cancelled request's POST is cut before the cancellation is sent; a redirect is followed only within the origin (307/308), so credentials never reach another host; an error names the status and Retry-After, never the reply's body (D212 still reads a 429 from it; a non-429 whose first 512 bytes say "rate limit" or "too many requests" is marked `rate limited` in fixed words). The server side is a hand-written handler (`initialize`, `ping`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, a literal JSON Schema, hand validation; a bad argument, an unknown tool or a failed ask is an `isError` result, as the SDK's `McpServer` gave, and any other failure an InternalError) and a byte-level stdio transport with a 1 MiB line cap. McpSource keeps only the tools it uses while paging `tools/list` (stopping when all are found, on a repeated cursor, or after 20 pages or 10,000 tools), and its read-only check (D7) is unchanged. An independent security review's proofs of concept, before and after: an 8 MiB unended line in 4 KB chunks 1,622 → 12 ms; 1 KB writes with no line end 5,730 → 96 ms of CPU; 20,000 server requests on a reply 20,003 POSTs (20,000 pending, +80 MB) → the reply failed after 100, no POST for a non-ping; 20 repeated-cursor pages of 16 MiB 4.86M tools held, 756 MB RSS → refused at 4 MiB, 46 MB; 2.1M junk events 3,127 / 1,898 ms → 59 / 60 ms. Left out, none used by Eden: OAuth (credentials are the operator's static headers), the standalone GET stream and `Last-Event-ID` resumption, JSON-RPC batches (removed from MCP in 2025-06-18), the session DELETE (the SDK's `close` sends none), output-schema validation of `structuredContent` (Eden reads what it reads, untrusted either way), a stdio client (only the lab launches servers, with the SDK's). Amends D15's dependency list. | D1705 | 2026-11-13 | **Adopted (the owner's request; D1704's bar): Eden has no production npm dependency. The seven gitleaks rules that backtrack in JavaScript run on hand-written linear matchers and every allowlist regex on the gate's own lazy DFA; `re2js` 2.9.0 is a devDependency, the tests' oracle.** Amends D24 (its engine) and D15's dependency list. `packages/redact/src/scanners.ts` holds one matcher for the five keyword-assignment rules (cisco-meraki-api-key, cohere-api-token, okta-access-token, privateai-api-token, sumologic-access-id: `[\w.-]{0,50}?(?i:[\w.-]{0,50}?KW[ \t\w.-]{0,20}[\s'"]{0,3})OP[\x60'"\s=]{0,5}(SECRET)END`), anchored on keyword occurrences, and one for the two curl rules (`curl-auth-header`'s lazy path, `curl-auth-user`'s greedy one), anchored on `curl` and on option positions. Each reports RE2's leftmost-first match and every group span, argued from RE2's match order in the file (the leftmost start is the least start any keyword's lazy runs reach; a curl match takes the first option in the path's order whose rest matches), with memos (operator positions, the next or previous matching option, the multi-line walk by line break and depth, the run of characters a keyword's suffix reads) so each position is examined a bounded number of times. Memory follows the matches, not the text's length: the position memos are fixed-size and direct-mapped (4,096 slots, none for a text under 4,096 characters), options take 8 bytes each in typed arrays, and group spans are kept only for the first match (the review found the first version held a memo slot per character and depth: 1,068 MB on 16 MB of match-dense curl text, against 104 MB on re2js). Each names the exact regex it implements, and `rulesWith` throws when the vendored rule's regex differs (`checkScanners`): a gitleaks update that changes one fails every test and stops the gate building, never running a matcher written for another regex. It also parses every rule's own allowlist regexes (`checkAllowlists`), so an unsupported one stops the build too, not the first text its rule fires on. `automaton.ts` parses the RE2 subset the allowlists use (classes, escapes, POSIX classes, `(?i)` by Unicode simple folding, `(?s)`, counted repeats, `^ $ \A \z \b \B`), builds a Thompson NFA and runs it as a lazily built DFA, `test` only, one pass over code points (at most 2,000 states a pattern, then the cache is dropped and rebuilt); a plain string is an `includes`; syntax outside the subset throws when it compiles, as do the forms RE2 refuses (`\x` with one hex digit, nested counted repeats over 1,000). Chosen over rewriting each of the 49 allowlist regexes as a JavaScript regex (each would need its own proof that it cannot backtrack, and a gitleaks change to one would run on JavaScript's engine unnoticed) or a hand check each: one engine, linear by construction, its exactness checked once per regex. Both keep the meanings D24 gave these regexes on re2js (`re2Source`, now in the test-only `re2-oracle.ts`): JavaScript's `\s`; `.` excludes `\n`, `\r`, U+2028 and U+2029 also under `(?s)` (so the kubernetes-secret-yaml match allowlist's `(?s:.)` does not cross lines, as before: an allowlist that excuses less, kept); `(?i)` matches U+017F for s and U+212A for k; text is read by code point, a lone surrogate as one. No intended divergence. `scripts/dockerfile.test.ts` now fails if a server imports any npm package; `re2-oracle.ts` and `differential.ts` are left out of the image. A Bloom filter has no false negatives, so the gloss is unchanged, and English traffic ("What's", "I've", "Sarah's": their clitics are Czech and Turkish function words) no longer reads the lexicons. At the lazy read an I/O failure (no file, another size, a short read) glosses nothing for that request and is tried again by a later one; a changed prefix, a CRC or a table that reads wrong glosses nothing for the rest of the process; each is told once in a content-free line. On open, not in `rehomeSourceMaps` before children start: the open is the one place every file passes (mcp-stdio and one process have no rehome when nothing is stranded), and N children move their own files in parallel. Fail open: a file it cannot move (another connection holds the write lock past `MIGRATE_BUSY_MS`, 250 ms; read-only; disk full; damaged; columns not the map's, as an October 27 file's `last_ref`, which is never moved and logs its line at every open; an index, trigger or view made outside Eden naming its tables, which the drop would lose or the rename trip on; too little free disk; more than `MIGRATE_MAX_PAGES`, 32,768 pages, 128 MiB; or past `MIGRATE_BUDGET_MS`) keeps its rowid layout, unchanged, with one log line an open, and works as before; nothing throws. Disk room, checked before the lock with `statfs` on the file's directory and on SQLite's temp directory (where VACUUM writes its copy): free space at least 2x the file plus its WAL plus 4 MiB when the two are one filesystem, else 1.5x beside the file and 1x in the temp directory (measured 1.48x, 1.0x and 0.47x): without it a move that committed and then failed its VACUUM left a 1.5x file and a full disk where the old file had kept working. A VACUUM that fails or is skipped still truncates the WAL in its own try, and a later open compacts the file (a file with no rowid table and free pages at least a quarter of it and 256 pages, live pages at most half the cap, room as above; `compacted` or `not compacted` in one line). Bounded by time as well as size: the copy runs in key-ordered batches of 4,096 rows and reads the clock between batches and tables, rolling the whole move back past `MIGRATE_BUDGET_MS` (3 s), and VACUUM runs only if the move took at most half of it, so a router's children moving at once (D172's 30 s start deadline) each spend at most about 3.5 s; `bun packages/graph/src/migrate.ts FILE` moves a larger or slower file with the server stopped, with no size or time bound, and says `no source-map tables` (exit 1) for a file that is not a map. Nothing is served during it: one process and a router child open the map before they listen or report their port (a router listens only once every child has), mcp-stdio before it reads stdin. | D1975 | 2026-11-18 | **Adopted: a follow-up also carries what the previous turn delivered, not only the request's words.** `carry` (partner.ts) blends in the content terms of the items the followed request's answer sent (`Session.delivered` gains `turn` and `terms`, bounded per item, title first): "order", "shipped", "arrives" live on the item handed, not in the request's words, so "and the cable?" after the headphones order reached the sibling order 874 where D1973's request-term carry still scored below the candidates' cutoff. | D1985 | 2026-11-19 | **Adopted: a turn that asks starts the push when nothing started it — `pushAsk` — and Hermes names `ask_context` on a packetless question.** The v0.3.0 broad benchmark's decisive correlation: an injected turn scored 85% correct against 17% where nothing was injected — under deferred tools the agent rarely discovers `ask_context` on its own, so a question the gate stays silent on was a near-certain miss (16% of question turns). Two model-free arms close it. In the engine, `pushAsk` (default, part `ask`): a sent user message that starts no push — the rule has none or the gate vetoed it — starts an `opened` one when `asksQuestion` reads it as asking (the gate's `ask`/`qact` kind, or the message's own question shape: a leading wh-/yes-no word or a closing `?`, past `ASKS_OWN`'s narrower `listed` shape of D1980); a turn the gate reads as chatter is left alone, and with no gate the shape alone decides. The question is itself the lookup's request: the started push is an ordinary opened one, so the candidates' own constraint-like gate still decides whether anything goes and silence stays the default — the start widens recall without touching the false-fire bar. In the Hermes plugin, the floor that stays: a question-shaped message that got no packet gets `ASK_HINT`, a one-line nudge naming `ask_context` (`EDEN_ASK_HINT=0` off), so the agent is told of the tool the deferred bridge hid even when the push found nothing. `bun run eval`: precision 0.9074, recall 0.98, falseFireRate 0. | D2015 | 2026-11-20 | **Adopted: a static per-connector-kind prior reshapes a cold source's routing draw (Q7(b) of `docs/research/o4-new-user.md`).** `sourceKindPrior` (default 20) seeds each source's Beta draw before it has outcomes of its own: a source whose id or description names a kind a person's requests usually land in — mail, calendar, contacts — draws from `Beta(1 + strength*mean, 1 + strength*(1-mean))` (`SOURCE_KIND_PRIOR`), and every other source draws from `Beta(1, 1 + strength/2)` (mean 0). | D2009 | 2026-11-20 | **Adopted: a per-user alias table — name parts to their full names — expands a request's anchors, so a person asked for by one form anchors to items naming them by another.** Built at ingest from the items' `partiesOf` tally (a mail's From/To/Cc, an event's attendees, `meta.people`): `UserCache.aliases` maps each lowercased name part to the full names holding it ("webb" → {"marcus webb"}), computed lazily like `personNames` and reset by the same tally. At request time `aliasExpand` (settle.ts) grows the cue's entities through `ItemCache.aliasTable`: a multi-word name adds each non-first part the table joins to that same name ("Marcus Webb" → "webb", so the "Webb contract" item anchors it), and a lone part adds each full name holding it ("webb" → "marcus webb", so a participant-only item anchors it). The partner's five `anchorsOf` sites go through `requestAnchors`. The table only joins parts that share a full name, so a non-person entity gains nothing; expansion is capped at 8 extra entities. Q1.1 of `docs/research/weak-points-1111.md`: the alias axes that need no model (name parts); roles ("my dentist" → "Dr Patel") stay unbuilt — no mapping exists in the items. | D1984 | 2026-11-18 | **Adopted: a request may re-search its sources once, bounded and counted, for companions the cache never saw — `companionSearch`.** `companions` (D1977) could only link what the request's own words had already fetched into the scored pool or the item cache, so a companion a search never returned stayed a miss (the meeting's agenda doc, the order's returns policy). Behind `companionSearch` (default 4 sources, `companionSearchMs` 400) the companion pass now asks the sources once more, on a text built from the picks' link terms and refs, sanitized like any text leaving the engine: one bounded search call per source, each page stored as it settles so a slow connector never hides the others' finds, and only a page that reached its source is stored — a fan-out cache page was already stored under its own read mark, its calls added to the lookup's `sourceCalls` through `withCompanions`' `onCalls`, so the lab's per-task sum still equals what the connectors counted. What comes back is stored like any lookup read (`Tracer.page` keeps its sanitize/cache spans under the new `search.behind` async span), then read back through the normal cache search and the same `take` gate every companion takes — `contradicts`, bulk mail, `isFresh`, `sameRef`, `alreadyHas`, the per-pick link — so the pool still decides and silence-by-default holds. Serving never waits on it: the pass waits at most `companionSearchMs`; calls settling later are stored for the next read and get a trace of their own, as a search behind does. A source the sync reads is never re-searched (`sync.isWarm`): its current copy is already in the cache the first pass searched, and a poll in flight reads its boundary off what is stored — a re-search's finds held early would fake that boundary and truncate the poll. Hits read back from beyond the scored pool must prove a stricter link (`needReq`): a shared identifier, one shared link word beside a request word or a whole shared entity, or two rare shared words only when the hit is of another source than the pick — two shared words inside one sender's mail are sender noise, not a link. Two link fixes ship with it, since the re-search reads hits the pool never filtered: a word written capitalized on both sides counts as a link word only beside request evidence (a shared proper name like "Lakeland"; common capitalized words like "Perfect"/"Reply" are noise, and the redaction placeholder never binds), and a two-letter code of a letter and a digit ("q3" of a board pack) counts as a link term where the three-letter bar dropped it. Around the same misses: a stop-word-only message that is question-shaped ("Right. Who is he again?") is no longer dropped as chatter — it reaches `carry`, where the pronoun-person handling (D1983) reads the follow-up as about the last request's person; `fallback`'s named-person search prefers the record whose title is just the name (the contact card) over mails merely naming them on "who is" questions; and a `clash` answer puts the clashing items first and keeps the request's subject items beside them — the booking being moved is as much the answer as the train it would sit on. `bun run eval`: precision 0.90 -> 0.9074, recall 0.90 -> 0.98 (49 of 50), falseFireRate 0. | D2033 | 2026-11-21 | **Adopted: the v0.3.0 broad-benchmark harness lives in the repo as `packages/sim/lab/fresh-corpus`, regenerated per quarter (build item 4).** A benchmark run on a corpus the model may have memorised measures memory, not retrieval, so the eval's corpus is generated, never committed: `gen_corpus.py --seed 20261119` reproduces the v0.3.0 reference byte for byte (553 docs, all 73 scored questions verified equal), and any other seed keeps the same shape while perturbing the persona, amounts, dates-of-month and codes through a facts layer shared by doc text and gold answers. `drive_eval.py` is the free hook-level gate (injection recall, ask_context accuracy, neutral false fires, latency, party check); `ab_run.py` + `score_ab.py` the paid A/B vs a file-search control; `soak.py` latency and RSS drift. Paid runs re-check the owner's spend opt-in (`EDEN_ALLOW_OPENROUTER=1`) since the Bun lab-guard cannot reach plain Python. | `gen_corpus.py` output verified equal to the v0.3.0 corpus on the default seed; `score_ab.py` reproduces the published A/B tallies from the original run records. |

| D2035 | 2026-11-21 | **Adopted: an explicit ask's words read as OR-groups — each content word's stem-family in the index plus its phrasing family (`ASK_FAMILY`) — with coverage credited once per group at the group's rarest variant's idf (`askExpand`).** The exact-word index was read in the item's own writing, so a question asked differently missed what it meant: "who manages my flat / emergency number" found nothing on "Landlord agent … emergencies 020 7946 0331", "how much rent do I pay each month" ranked an HMRC letter over the Monzo standing order, "mortgage rate and monthly payment" missed the offer. Each question word now seeds one OR-group — its own term when a live doc holds it (so "wi-fi" stays one term), the index's terms sharing its stem ("emergency" meets "emergencies"), and the family's words ("manag" meets "agent", "rent" meets "rental/landlord/letting") — a word the index never saw still gets its family, and a freed term is left out since its idf would weigh against the survivors. The search reads the union at a wider 48 (a doc dense in one word's variants cannot crowd out the rare topic word), then each group's rarest-variant idf credits a doc holding any of its variants once: a synonym's common-word repeats cannot outscore the question's topic. Explicit `ask` calls only — `internal.push` reads stay on the exact-word path, so the proactive false-fire rate is untouched; misses still answer plainly with no expansion to confuse them. `bun run eval` unchanged: precision 0.9074, recall 0.98 (49/50), falseFireRate 0. Broad-benchmark misses fixed on this branch: q32 mortgage rate+payment, q39 who-manages+emergency-number, q55 how-much-rent. | `ask-expand.test.ts`: 4 replays — the emergency-number phrasing now finds home-admin, rent ranks the statement over the tax letter, wi-fi keeps its compound match, and flag-off keeps the miss; eval and the full check suite rerun. |


| D2036 | 2026-11-21 | **Adopted: staleness is read of the document, at day and month granularity, and applied to every pick — `docSpan`, `expiryOf`, `staleSelf`, `staleSibling` (generalizes D1982).** Superseded, expired and revised records could still lead a packet or an answer beside their current copy (v0.3.0 broad benchmark, build item 3). A record is now dated by `docSpan`: `meta.start`, or the title's own dates — ISO, "13 November 2026", "November 13, 2026", "March 2026", a bare month after a separator ("— September"), bare years, then the body's years when the title names none; a yearless date resolves to the occurrence nearest the day it was written (`updatedAt ?? cue.at`, never the wall clock — the eval's clock stays deterministic). `expiryOf` reads the deadline an `EXPIRY_LEAD` match names ("offer ends 30 September", "expires November"); a yearless deadline is the first such date on or after the write day, a bare month its own end. `staleSelf` marks a record dead when it declares itself ("[OLD]", "(superseded)", "no longer valid", "superseded by") or its named deadline is past — resolved once per item (`staleMemo`), so a yearless deadline already past does not roll into next year on a later request. `staleSibling` marks an anchored record dead when every entity it anchors to carries a newer approved record in the pool or among items already delivered — per entity, the newest span start wins. Both rules stand down when the request itself dates what it wants (`ASKS_OLD`, a literal year, or a month name in the raw words — "balance on 30 September?" asks for September's record), and a timed item is never the stale sibling. Applied across the board: `candidatesOf`' fast path, `confident`, `grounded`'s pool, `subject` picks, `companions`, `fallback`, and `partner-ask` ordering. `bun run eval`: precision 0.9074, recall 0.98, falseFireRate 0 — unchanged; on unseen superseded/expired/revised documents 21 of 21 scenarios pass where 8 of the first 13 did before. | `stale-supersession.test.ts`: 22 replays — flagged-old statements, body-declared supersession, past-deadline offers, revised tariffs, a request naming the record's month or year, a revision published ahead of its month, a person named May, a month-only deadline, a separator day-month-year keeping its year; eval and `CHECK_COLD=1 bun run check` rerun (one pre-existing `source-calls.test.ts` failure reproduces on clean `main`). |
| D2037 | 2026-11-21 | **Adopted: a pace per (tenant, connector) shared by the tenant's users, configured by `tenantCallsPerMin` and holding only background reads.** B1 of docs/research/s1-scale-1m.md: a connector's quota is the tenant's, but Eden paced per (user, source) only, so a surge spent the shared quota on deep pages and the connector's 429s hit users at random. `SourceFanout` keeps a second GCRA keyed `${tenantId}|${sourceId}` when `tenantRatePerSec` is set (0 in the default: nothing changes, per the pre-registered bar). Every admitted call — search, fetch, plan call, listing — charges it, so real load counts; only `list` calls carrying `reserve` (the sync's background pages) are refused when it is spent, so a lookup's own poll, search and fetch are never held. The connector's own 429 penalizes the tenant bucket from every call path, pushing the whole tenant's background calls back, not one user's; per-user and shadow limits are untouched. `guarded.test.ts`: a tenant's second background listing is `limited` while its demand calls and another tenant pass, and one user's search 429 limits the tenant's next background page — both falsified without the bucket. |
| D2038 | 2026-11-21 | **Adopted: a kicked step's freed turn goes to the waiting tenants in turn, not to the first-come queue.** `kickDue` kept one FIFO `kickQueue` across tenants, so a surge from one tenant (a deploy connecting thousands of its users at once) made every other tenant's new user wait behind all of it — B2 of docs/research/s1-scale-1m.md, the first piece of the S1 plan that ships alone. The waiters are now held one list per tenant in a `Map`; each dequeue moves the served tenant's list to the back, so a waiting tenant's first user starts before a served tenant's second. Within a tenant the order is still first-come; the same-user and per-source caps are untouched. `sync-kick.test.ts` orders four running + three waiting of one tenant against a late arrival of another: the late tenant starts second, not last — falsified by restoring the shared FIFO. |
| D2039 | 2026-11-21 | **Adopted: a tight tenant pace is spent in value order — a background read's `tier` asks more of the bucket be free.** The rest of S1-P1 (`docs/research/s1-scale-1m.md` §3): the pace alone left the connector's calls first-come — a sweep could win the tokens a new user's first pages needed. Each background `list` now names a tier — first page, poll, deeper backfill, sweep — and the tenant bucket admits it only when `tenantNeed(tier)` tokens are free: `1 + floor((burst − 1) × tier / 3)`, so a first page goes whenever any token exists while a sweep goes only at a nearly full bucket, and no queue or reorder is needed. Demand calls (a lookup's own poll, search, fetch) still carry no reserve and are never held. `sync.ts` labels its five reserved call sites; `guarded.test.ts` shows three of four tokens spent admits the first page but holds the poll, deeper page and sweep — falsified with the tier ignored. |
| D2040 | 2026-11-21 | **Adopted: the sync's backfill and fairness signals in `/metrics` (S1-P2).** B4 of docs/research/s1-scale-1m.md: users backfilling, the kick queue, time to first value and connector 429s were invisible, leaving nothing for an autoscaler or an SLO to read. The scrape now exports gauges `eden_sync_users_backfilling` (a source still in its first pass), `eden_sync_users_waiting_first_page` (the backlog's measure), `eden_sync_kick_queue_users`/`_tenants`/`_kick_running`, counters `eden_sync_listing_{calls,held,throttled}_total{tier}` (the pace's holds and the connector's 429s per priority, plus `tier="demand"`), and the histogram `eden_sync_first_value_seconds` (first event → first stored page). First value is recorded in `store` — `polledAt` cannot mark it, since it moves only when a whole first pass ends (`warmUp`), pages past the cap included. All counters sit on `SyncStats` (the trace log's object) and are read by `Ops.metrics` through `partner.sync`; a user a process never tracked contributes nothing. Counts only, no tenant or user labels (D56's rule). `sync-metrics.test.ts`: the gauges, the tier counters and the histogram each falsified by removing their recorder. |
| D2041 | 2026-11-21 | **Adopted: the shutdown drain writes live users most recently seen first, in a lean blob that leaves the index and vocabulary out (`LEAN_MAGIC` "EDF3").** S1-P3 of docs/research/s1-scale-1m.md: `flush` wrote warm blobs in insertion order, at ~9 ms a user (1,500 items, measured), so a full box's drain overran the ~4.5 s `persistLive` share of the shutdown grace, and whoever the Map happened to order last paid the re-sync. The lean form is the fast form's layout without `index.snapshot()`/`vocab.snapshot()`, their arrays or `gaps` — ~5.5 ms a user — and `flush` now walks `users` in `seen`-descending order, so a deadline strands the coldest users (the cheapest to re-sync, or never asked for). Its thaw rebuilds the index and vocabulary from the items' texts like a compact thaw does — sliced, on the first read after the restart — while the packed texts still cross the blob uncompressed (`packedFrom`, no re-pack; ~29 ms vs the compact thaw's ~35 ms at 1,500 items). The drain blob gets its own magic rather than a flag in "EDF2", so `FrozenUser.warm` stays honest — a lean blob does not thaw in milliseconds — and an older binary reads it as neither form and starts the user over. `release` still writes the full warm form: a hand-off moves one user, and the new owner's thaw speed is the point of it. `persist.test.ts`: the drain test captures the written blob's EDF3 magic and spies zero index/vocabulary snapshots during `flush`, the ordering test records write order (bob seen a tick later than alice is written first); each falsified — warm-form flush, no lean thaw dispatch, insertion order. |
| D2042 | 2026-11-21 | **Adopted: `EDEN_PERSIST_STORE` may name several buckets, comma-separated; a user's shard is their bucket mod the count.** S1-P4 of docs/research/s1-scale-1m.md (B6): Hetzner Object Storage allows ~750 requests a second per bucket, which a 1M fleet's peak — and any rebalance that must write its moved users inside the router's 60 s bound — exceeds. `ShardedBlobStore` (persist-shared.ts) routes each key by the first four hex digits of the blob name, which are the user's bucket, so a shard's traffic is a shard's share of the fleet; a key naming no blob (the `key-id` marker) sits on the first store, and `list` merges the shards so the age sweep and the key check's sample still span every copy. Every URL must share one prefix (a key's shard is picked by bucket, the name under the prefix unchanged); credentials and endpoint are shared. Changing the shard count moves every user: a fetch looks in the new shard's bucket, misses the copy written under the old count, and the user re-syncs while the orphaned copy ages out through the merged sweep — so the count is set once and changed in a quiet window. `ShardedBlobStore` lives beside `SharedFrozenDisk` so any `BlobStore` impl shards; `S3BlobStore` now takes one bucket's config. `persist-shared.test.ts`: blobs land only in their bucket's shard, the marker and merged list verified; falsified by routing every key to shard 0. `blob-store.test.ts`: the comma-separated parse and the shared-prefix refusal, falsified by dropping the check. |

| D2044 | 2026-11-21 | **Adopted: a node's release bound scales with the users it is expected to move (S1-P6).** The membership message carries the router's `deadlineMs` (per node: `rebalanceMs` + the moved-bucket share x the held count the node last reported x `releasePerUserMs`, default 15 ms); the node plans its release and its store writes inside `max(releaseMs, deadlineMs - 2 s)` (the floor keeps an older router's behavior, the slack the answer itself), and answers its `held` count so the next estimate bases itself on a fresh count. A big move used to hit the flat `rebalanceMs` bound, go silent mid-write, and be taken out as `reset` — its users dropped, not handed over. |
| D2046 | 2026-11-21 | **Adopted: a process-wide `RateHold` shared by the model roles — a 429 holds every caller, and a call made while held fails fast without sending.** S1-P9 of docs/research/s1-scale-1m.md: OpenRouter's rate limit applies to the whole account, so without a shared hold each role kept burning requests against a limit that was already answering 429 — each such call cost a full timeout against the engine's own deadlines and piled more requests into the limited window. `RateHold` in `@eden/llm` records the server's asked delay (`retry-after-ms`, `Retry-After`, `x-ratelimit-reset`) or a jittered doubling backoff over the 429 streak (capped at 60 s, cleared by an answered call); `modelRolesFromEnv` hands one instance to all three roles; `OpenRouterModel.chat` throws `ModelHeldError` at once while held. The engine takes its no-model path as on any throw (D41); a held call counts under `eden_model_failures_total{kind="held"}` — separate from `error`, which the `EdenModelFailing` alert reads — and is never logged. `llm.test.ts`: a 429 holds the sibling role, the held call sends nothing, and calls resume after the delay — falsified by disabling the gate. |

| D2043 | 2026-11-21 | **Adopted: a dry-run autoscale plan — `deploy/scripts/autoscale-plan.py` reads `/metrics` from every node, plans a node count with hysteresis and a peak-hour guard, and prints the tofu varset and nodes-file lines to apply by hand.** S1-P5 of docs/research/s1-scale-1m.md (B5): scaling waits on someone reading dashboards and doing §6's arithmetic by hand. The planner scrapes the gauges P2 ships (`eden_users_held`, `eden_process_resident_bytes`, `eden_processes_ready`, the kick queue and first-page backlog), measures the live per-user cost from the fullest node (floor `--rss-per-user`, the peak soak's 4.71 MB), and plans `projected = users x --peak-factor` (peaks run ~22% over the mean, D1075) against the same sizing formula `sizing.py` prints — so the plan and the doc never disagree on what a box holds. Scale-out is immediate and unbounded by hysteresis (a node over 85% RSS adds one whatever the math says); scale-in needs `--confirm-in` consecutive below-need readings and never runs inside `--peak-hours` (a scale-in at peak cuts capacity before the day's high). One reading moves at most `--max-move-frac` (10%) of nodes — P6's step bound. A node that does not answer counts as full, so missing data only ever adds. `--metrics-dir` reads saved scrapes for tests and postmortems; `--cidr` renders the `cidrhost(N+11)` nodes-file lines the tofu nodes output implies. It is a plan, never an actor: nothing mutates — the operator applies `node_count` and the nodes file. `autoscale-plan.test.ts`: scale-out under load bounded to a tenth, the consecutive-readings gate releasing on the third, the peak-hours hold, a down node never shrinking, the 0-user bloated node forcing +1 through the urgent clause, and the cidr render — falsified by removing the urgent clause and the peak block. |

## Trial switches

A trial is decided in the branch or session that opened it, as soon as its evidence is in (D814): promoted into
`DEFAULT_CONFIG` (measured better or neutral at no extra paid cost) or deleted with its code and tests. No end date
weeks out and no "owner's call later"; where a cost trade-off remains, the session recommends and the parent decides
that day. A row here is a trial whose evidence is still being gathered by the session that opened it. The push-check
trials were decided by D828 (promoted or deleted), so none is left here.

| Trial | Switch | Owner | Ends | What decides it |
| ----- | ------ | ----- | ---- | --------------- |
